correctness.rationale: Direct neighbour counts give the exact parity-split core update. For even order the balanced-core swap set and homogeneous states exhaust recurrence; for odd order disjoint/cover borderline pairs exhaust recurrence. Binomial counting gives all four depth populations and exact fixed/primitive-two-cycle numbers. Sharpness is proved, including \(m=3\), and Stirling gives asymptotics. A separate direct-neighbourhood exhaustive program checked all 349504 labelled configurations for \(m=3\) through 9, corroborating but not replacing the universal proof.

Previous exact majority results on split graphs and clique windmills use different graph neighbourhoods; neither graph class contains K_m∘K_1 as a member for m≥3.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A universal bound on eventual period does not imply the sharp transient bound or orbit multiplicities. In a complete split graph every pendant-class node connects to every clique node, while here each leaf connects to exactly one. In a clique windmill the outer vertices lie in cliques with a shared hub, whereas here the clique has m private degree-one leaves. The cases are structurally nonreducible under neighbourhood-preserving conjugacies.

value.rationale: A clique corona is a canonical dense consensus network with one private memory leaf at each voter. The result is a complete natural infinite-family attractor and first-periodic-time classification. The polynomial-versus-exponential recurrence split between even and odd clique order, exact primitive two-cycle census, and factor-two asymptotic maximal-delay disparity are meaningful quantitative structural phenomena not implied by generic period-two theorems. This is not a tiny parameter gain or finite table recomputation.
